phases.name: Route players to regional game sessions
phases.description: Place global routing and matchmaking before regional GKE game-server allocation and explicit session lifecycle management.

phases.name: Keep authoritative records correct
phases.description: Separate strongly consistent durable state and transactions from the low-latency regional gameplay loop, and validate untrusted actions server-side.

phases.name: Derive live ranking and health
phases.description: Use events to build live leaderboard views, cache hot rankings, and make game-server health observable while calling out global-consistency tradeoffs.

phases.name: Connect gameplay, persistence, and events
phases.description: Connect session placement, server-authoritative actions, durable transactions, and asynchronous ranking and telemetry paths.

phases.name: Validate latency and availability targets
phases.description: Treat global latency, one-million concurrency, 100k matches per second, and five-nines state availability as targets that require workload and failure testing.

steps.phase: Route players to regional game sessions
steps.title: Freeze the exact problem brief
steps.content:
Title: Build a Global Gaming Backend System
Description: Design a low-latency gaming backend that handles millions of concurrent players, provides real-time matchmaking, stores player data globally, and manages game sessions.
Requirements:
1. Handle player matchmaking
2. Store game state globally
3. Implement real-time leaderboards
4. Process in-game transactions
5. Handle game session management
6. Implement anti-cheat mechanisms
7. Support cross-region gameplay
8. Monitor game server performance
Constraints:
1. Latency under 50ms globally
2. Support 1M+ concurrent players
3. Strong consistency for transactions
4. 99.999% availability for game state
5. Handle 100k+ matches per second
Hints:
1. Cloud Spanner for global consistency
2. Memorystore Redis for caching
3. GKE for game servers
4. Cloud Load Balancing for routing
5. Agones for game server orchestration
6. Cloud Pub/Sub for event streaming

steps.phase: Route players to regional game sessions
steps.title: Route each player toward a healthy nearby region
steps.content: Use the hinted global Cloud Load Balancing role to direct players to an appropriate healthy regional entry point. Session affinity and UDP/TCP protocols depend on the game transport, which the brief does not specify.

component.label: Global Game Traffic Load Balancer
component.description: Global routing to healthy regional game and matchmaking entry points.

properties.purpose: Route player connections to healthy regional game and matchmaking services using the selected transport protocol; protocol, affinity, and region policy require game-specific validation.

component.highlightReason: Cross-region gameplay and global latency need an explicit traffic-routing layer.

steps.phase: Route players to regional game sessions
steps.title: Match players by compatible game and region
steps.content: Keep matchmaking separate from live simulation. It can select compatible players, modes, and a region using queue age, skill, party constraints, and measured latency; exact fairness and wait-time objectives are unspecified.

component.label: Regional Matchmaking Service
component.description: Forms compatible matches and selects an eligible regional game fleet.

properties.purpose: Group compatible players and choose an eligible region/fleet using game rules and measured latency; define fairness, queue-wait, and party policies from product requirements.

component.highlightReason: Player matchmaking is a core requirement and should not be mixed into the latency-sensitive game simulation loop.

steps.phase: Route players to regional game sessions
steps.title: Allocate regional game servers through GKE
steps.content: Use GKE with a game-server orchestrator such as Agones to provision, allocate, and recycle game-server processes. Fleet warm capacity, scale-up time, and regional quotas must be measured against match arrival bursts.

component.label: GKE Game-Server Fleet (Agones)
component.description: Regional container orchestration and game-server allocation.

properties.purpose: Orchestrate regional game-server processes and allocation using GKE with an Agones-style fleet controller; tune warm capacity and scale behavior from measured match bursts and startup time.

component.highlightReason: GKE and Agones are hinted for game-server orchestration and match capacity management.

steps.phase: Route players to regional game sessions
steps.title: Keep real-time simulation close to the players
steps.content: Run authoritative game simulation on regional servers so movement and short-lived session state do not require a global strongly consistent write on every tick. Persist durable checkpoints and business events separately; server capacity must be load tested.

component.label: Regional Authoritative Game Servers
component.description: Low-latency regional simulation and server-authoritative gameplay.

properties.purpose: Run authoritative regional simulation and short-lived session state near connected players; persist durable progression at defined boundaries rather than synchronously writing every simulation tick globally.

component.highlightReason: The global under-50ms goal conflicts with routing every game-state update through a cross-region strong-consistency transaction.

steps.phase: Route players to regional game sessions
steps.title: Track session allocation and lifecycle
steps.content: Represent session creation, join tokens, heartbeat/lease, reconnect, completion, and cleanup as an explicit control path. Session ownership and migration behavior across regions need game-specific rules; do not move a live session without an agreed consistency model.

component.label: Game Session Manager
component.description: Session lifecycle, player membership, and allocated-server coordination.

properties.purpose: Create and track sessions, player membership, allocation leases, reconnect windows, and completion; cross-region migration and recovery semantics depend on game rules.

component.highlightReason: Session lifecycle and reconnect behavior are explicit requirements, distinct from the real-time simulation process.

steps.title: Keep durable global player and match records in Spanner
steps.content: Use the hinted Cloud Spanner role for globally durable records that require relational transactions and strong consistency. Data partitioning, multi-region configuration, contention, and write latency must be measured; do not assume every ephemeral game-state update belongs here.

component.label: Cloud Spanner Durable Game State
component.description: Globally durable player, match, and transaction records.

properties.purpose: Persist durable player progression, match outcomes, and transaction records with the required strong-consistency boundary; region topology, schema, capacity, and write latency require workload validation.

component.highlightReason: Cloud Spanner is hinted for global consistency, while its use on every realtime simulation tick would put the 50ms goal at risk.

steps.title: Isolate strongly consistent in-game transactions
steps.content: Use an explicit transaction service for purchases, rewards, and other value-changing operations. Validate ownership and balance, apply idempotency keys, and atomically update the durable ledger/state; define retry and duplicate-submission behavior.

component.label: In-Game Transaction Service
component.description: Validated, idempotent transaction workflow for player value changes.

properties.purpose: Validate and authorize value-changing operations, use idempotency keys, and atomically persist ledger and player-state updates; define retry, duplicate, and reconciliation behavior.

component.highlightReason: Transactions explicitly require strong consistency, so they need a narrow authoritative path rather than best-effort cache updates.

steps.title: Validate gameplay on trusted servers
steps.content: Treat clients as untrusted: validate legal actions, movement bounds, cooldowns, and transaction eligibility on the server; combine deterministic rules with risk signals and review. The brief does not specify anti-cheat threat model or acceptable false-positive rate.

component.label: Server-Side Anti-Cheat Validation
component.description: Validates gameplay actions and emits suspicious-behavior signals.

properties.purpose: Validate gameplay and transaction actions against authoritative server state and game rules, record risk signals, and support review without trusting client-reported outcomes.

component.highlightReason: Anti-cheat is explicit; enforcement belongs on trusted server paths rather than client-only checks.

steps.title: Publish completed-match and gameplay events asynchronously
steps.content: Use Pub/Sub to decouple post-match events, leaderboard aggregation, and operational consumers from the simulation request path. Events need stable match/player identifiers and duplicate-safe consumers; event retention and ordering are not specified.

component.label: Cloud Pub/Sub Match Events
component.description: Asynchronous event stream for completed matches and derived views.

properties.purpose: Distribute identified match and gameplay events to ranking and operational consumers without blocking the real-time simulation path; consumer processing must tolerate redelivery.

component.highlightReason: Pub/Sub is hinted for event streaming and keeps leaderboard aggregation and analytics off the gameplay critical path.

steps.title: Aggregate completed-match events into leaderboard updates
steps.content: Process score and match events with deduplication and an explicit ranking-window policy. The brief says real-time but does not define ranking freshness, global versus regional board scope, or tie-breaking rules.

component.label: Leaderboard Aggregation Worker
component.description: Consumes match outcomes and computes ranking updates asynchronously.

properties.purpose: Consume identified match outcomes, deduplicate events, and calculate ranking updates outside the simulation path; freshness, board scope, and tie-breaking rules require product decisions.

component.highlightReason: An asynchronous aggregator protects gameplay latency while enabling near-real-time leaderboard updates.

steps.title: Cache hot leaderboard views in Redis
steps.content: Use Memorystore Redis for low-latency reads of hot ranking slices, while preserving a durable/rebuildable ranking source and explicit update semantics. Cache eviction or region loss should not destroy authoritative player state.

component.label: Memorystore Redis Leaderboard Cache
component.description: Fast regional reads for hot leaderboard windows.

properties.purpose: Serve hot leaderboard slices with low read latency while treating cached rankings as rebuildable views and keeping durable player/match records in the authoritative store.

component.highlightReason: Memorystore Redis is hinted for caching and supports fast leaderboard reads without replacing durable game state.

steps.title: Instrument game servers and regional dependencies
steps.content: Monitor session allocation, active players, match-start rate, server tick health, disconnects, regional network latency, Spanner transaction latency/errors, and event/leaderboard lag. Define game-specific health and page thresholds from an observed baseline.

component.label: Game Fleet and Match SLO Monitoring
component.description: Regional game-server, match, transaction, and event health signals.

properties.componentName: Game Fleet and Match SLO Monitoring
properties.purpose: Observe player/session counts, matchmaking throughput, game-server health and tick behavior, regional latency, transaction outcomes, and event/leaderboard lag for SLO and capacity evaluation.

component.highlightReason: Game-server monitoring is required and supplies evidence for concurrency, match throughput, latency, and availability.

steps.title: Separate the fast regional loop from global commits
steps.content: A globally strongly consistent write can add cross-region coordination latency, so the under-50ms global gameplay target and strong transactional consistency are in tension. Keep simulation/session state regional and ephemeral, and reserve Spanner transactions for durable business invariants and checkpoints. Whether that meets both goals must be measured in intended regions; do not claim the targets are automatically compatible.

steps.title: Route matchmaking requests to a healthy regional service
steps.content: Send queue and match-search requests to a healthy regional matchmaking service while retaining the ability to route players to another region when policy permits.

connection.label: regional matchmaking API
connection.description: Global routing forwards player match requests to healthy matchmaking capacity.

steps.title: Route established players to allocated game servers
steps.content: After allocation, route game traffic to its assigned regional server and validate reconnect/affinity behavior for the selected transport.

connection.label: player traffic to allocated server
connection.description: Global routing directs active player traffic to the healthy allocated regional game server.

steps.title: Serve leaderboard queries through a trusted game API
steps.content: The player-facing game API reads the cached ranking view; define authorization, board freshness, and regional fallback separately from transaction correctness.

connection.label: authorized ranking query
connection.description: The trusted game-server API reads the low-latency cached ranking view for connected players.

steps.title: Allocate a compatible game-server process
steps.content: Matchmaking asks the regional fleet controller to allocate a compatible server and returns the placement only after readiness checks pass.

connection.label: reserve ready game capacity
connection.description: Matchmaking selects and allocates an eligible ready server from the regional GKE/Agones fleet.

steps.title: Create a session record for the accepted match
steps.content: Persist session membership and allocation state with a recoverable identifier and lease so clients can join or reconnect under the defined policy.

connection.label: match membership and allocation
connection.description: Matchmaking creates session metadata and records the allocated server for player join/reconnect flows.

steps.title: Run the allocated simulation on the selected fleet
steps.content: The fleet controller launches and health-checks game-server processes before making them eligible for player allocation.

connection.label: ready regional simulation capacity
connection.description: GKE and the game-server controller schedule, health-check, and recycle regional game processes.

steps.title: Maintain session heartbeats and reconnect state
steps.content: Game servers report session lifecycle and health so the manager can expire abandoned leases, handle reconnect windows, and reconcile completed matches.

connection.label: lifecycle and completion events
connection.description: Regional simulation reports session health and completion to the session manager.

steps.title: Validate client actions against authoritative simulation
steps.content: Game servers pass suspicious or value-changing actions through server-side rule validation; the client never supplies the trusted final score or transaction outcome.

connection.label: validate gameplay actions
connection.description: Authoritative game state is checked against server-side rules and anti-cheat signals.

steps.title: Authorize value changes before committing them
steps.content: Only validated, authorized transaction intents reach the transaction service; preserve idempotency and reject or reconcile duplicate submissions.

connection.label: authorized and deduplicated action
connection.description: Gameplay validation passes eligible value-changing actions to the strongly consistent transaction workflow.

steps.title: Commit related transaction records atomically
steps.content: Use the database transaction boundary for ledger and player-state invariants; test retries, contention, and regional failover while measuring the latency impact.

connection.label: atomic ledger and player update
connection.description: The transaction service commits value-changing records with the required strong-consistency semantics in Spanner.

steps.title: Persist durable checkpoints, not every transient tick
steps.content: Write durable progression and match checkpoints at defined boundaries. Keep high-frequency ephemeral simulation state regional unless product consistency requirements prove a global synchronous write is necessary.

connection.label: match outcome and progression
connection.description: Regional game servers persist durable state transitions and completed outcomes without forcing every simulation tick through global consensus.

steps.title: Publish completed matches off the simulation path
steps.content: Emit identified completion and score events asynchronously after the authoritative outcome is accepted; downstream delivery can be retried without blocking player input.

connection.label: identified match outcomes
connection.description: Game servers publish accepted match outcomes and score events for asynchronous consumers.

steps.title: Retain durable session and match metadata
steps.content: Persist the durable session outcome and required membership/audit metadata, while keeping short-lived heartbeats and ephemeral state in a regional lifecycle layer.

connection.label: durable match metadata
connection.description: Session lifecycle persists the durable match and player outcome records needed for recovery and history.

steps.title: Consume match events for near-real-time rankings
steps.content: The ranking worker processes event IDs idempotently and applies the chosen board time window and ordering policy; monitor backlog as leaderboard freshness.

connection.label: match outcomes to ranking
connection.description: The leaderboard worker asynchronously consumes identified match events and computes ranking changes.

steps.title: Refresh the fast leaderboard view
steps.content: Publish ranking updates to Redis using an idempotent update strategy so a repeated event does not double-count scores.

connection.label: idempotent leaderboard refresh
connection.description: The aggregation worker updates the low-latency Redis leaderboard view from accepted match outcomes.

steps.title: Keep durable score outcomes rebuildable
steps.content: Persist canonical match results and any durable ranking inputs so the cached leaderboard can be rebuilt after regional cache loss; separate this write from transient score display updates.

connection.label: canonical score and outcome
connection.description: Accepted ranking inputs and match results are retained durably so Redis remains a rebuildable view.

steps.title: Observe match-event delivery and ranking freshness
steps.content: Track Pub/Sub delivery errors and worker backlog so delayed leaderboard updates are distinguishable from game-session failures.

connection.label: event delivery health
connection.description: Pub/Sub delivery metrics feed match-event and derived leaderboard freshness monitoring.

steps.title: Track fleet capacity and server performance
steps.content: Collect scheduling, readiness, allocation, server tick, and resource-saturation signals to validate the concurrency and match-rate targets across regions.

connection.label: allocation and game-server health
connection.description: GKE and game-server orchestration metrics expose fleet readiness, capacity, and performance.

steps.title: Alert on durable state and transaction SLOs
steps.content: Monitor Spanner availability, transaction latency, contention, aborts, and recovery signals; verify the five-nines objective against an explicit time window and failure model.

connection.label: global state and transaction health
connection.description: Spanner health and transaction outcomes feed state availability and strong-consistency SLO evaluation.

steps.title: Prove the global scale and game-state SLOs
steps.content: The brief does not define latency percentile, player geography, match duration, session-state write rate, transaction mix, failure domains, or the 99.999% measurement window. Load test at 1M concurrent players and 100k matches/second with realistic regional distributions; inject region loss, fleet exhaustion, network partitions, and transaction contention. Verify that durable state survives while regional gameplay remains responsive, and report any consistency/latency tradeoff rather than implying both targets are guaranteed.
